project_summary.north_star_kpi: Acceptance criteria of the approved requirements with a passing traced test: 74/80 today → 79/80. AC-015-004 (list prior backups and download the encrypted file) is deferred by the owner and remains the single untested AC after this feature.
project_summary.jtbd: As the sole admin of a headless Raspberry Pi, I hire Ultron-AP to tell me what my box is doing and let me act on it from one panel — without SSHing in, and without it waking me at 3am for a storm I already know about.
project_summary.guardrail_metric: Zero regressions: the 80 test cases passing today keep passing, and no new host action bypasses the privileged helper's allow-list.
project_summary.context: A coverage audit of the main pipeline (BL-033) found 41 acceptance criteria with no traced test. 35 were real behaviors that were merely untested and are now covered. The remaining 6 traced to behavior the approved requirements demand and the code never grew. This feature builds those six. It adds no new product surface beyond what FR-005, FR-006, FR-010, FR-013 and FR-015 already promise. The owner deferred the backup listing/download (parent AC-015-004) on 2026-07-13 and required the hardware controls to drive nothing, because a previous hardware-control attempt cost the Pi significant CPU and memory.

functional_requirements.title: Telegram mute window (1h / 4h / 24h)
functional_requirements.description: The admin can open a mute window of 1, 4 or 24 hours from Settings. While the window is open, alert notifications are not delivered to Telegram. The window expires on its own; the admin can also cancel it early. Extends FR-005 (Telegram notifications) and realises the parent's AC-005-005. The mute suppresses DELIVERY only — alerts keep firing, keep persisting to SQLite, and keep appearing in the Alerts panel and the alert-count SSE badge.
acceptance_criteria: With a mute window open (expires_at in the future), a fired alert produces zero Telegram send attempts — the notifier is not invoked.
With no mute window open, or with one whose expires_at has passed, a fired alert produces exactly one Telegram send attempt (unchanged FR-005 behaviour).
Selecting 1h / 4h / 24h persists a mute row whose expires_at equals the selection time plus 1 / 4 / 24 hours (±60s), surviving a process restart.
Cancelling an open window clears it, and the next fired alert is delivered to Telegram.
A muted alert is still written to the Alert table and still counted by the alert-count SSE event — mute never suppresses persistence or the in-panel view.
The Settings Telegram section shows the remaining mute time while a window is open, and a Mute/Cancel control otherwise.

functional_requirements.title: Daily email digest of the last 24h of alerts
functional_requirements.description: The admin can enable a daily digest and choose the hour (0–23) at which it is sent. At that hour, a single email summarising the previous 24 hours of alerts is delivered over the existing SMTP channel. Extends FR-006 (email notifications) and realises the parent's AC-006-004. The digest is additive: per-event alert emails keep sending exactly as they do today.
acceptance_criteria: With the digest enabled and the digest hour reached, exactly one email is sent, whose body lists the alerts created in the preceding 24 hours with their severity, source and timestamp.
The digest is sent at most once per calendar day: a second scheduler tick within the same hour of the same day sends nothing.
With zero alerts in the preceding 24h, the digest email is still sent once and states that no alerts fired (so silence is distinguishable from a broken digest).
With the digest disabled, the digest hour passing sends no email.
Per-event alert emails (FR-006) keep sending on every fire regardless of digest configuration.
The digest send is recorded in action_history so a failed send is observable without reading the journal.

functional_requirements.title: Per-service log drawer (last 100 journalctl lines)
functional_requirements.description: Each systemd service row on /services can expand a log drawer showing the last 100 journalctl lines for that unit, fetched through the privileged helper. Realises the parent's AC-010-002. The existing page-level /logs source dropdown (FR-010) is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a service row's log drawer issues one authenticated request that returns the last 100 journalctl lines for that unit, rendered inside the row.
The drawer request routes through the privileged helper's Unix socket with the unit name validated against the helper's allow-list — an injection-shaped name is rejected before any journalctl runs.
Log content is HTML-escaped and passes through the existing logfilter secret redaction, so a leaked token in the journal is not rendered to the browser.
When the helper is unavailable, the drawer renders an explicit error state with a message instead of an empty panel.
The drawer is closed by default: loading /services issues no journalctl fetch until the admin opens a drawer.

functional_requirements.title: Hardware section in Settings — fan mode
functional_requirements.description: The Settings page renders a hardware section containing a fan-mode selector (auto / quiet / performance / off) whose value persists. Realises the parent's AC-013-002. The panel does NOT drive the fan: the owner ran hardware control before and it cost the Pi significant CPU and memory, so this FR is the control surface plus its persisted value — a future actuator reads that value. Persisting a selection must add no polling loop, no daemon connection, and no per-request hardware I/O.
acceptance_criteria: The rendered /settings page contains a hardware section with a fan-mode selector offering exactly the modes auto, quiet, performance and off.
Saving a fan mode persists it and a subsequent page load renders that mode as the selected one, surviving a process restart.
A fan-mode value outside the four allowed modes is rejected with HTTP 400 and the stored value is unchanged.
Saving the hardware section without a valid CSRF token is rejected with HTTP 403 and nothing is persisted.
Saving or reading the fan mode performs no hardware I/O and starts no background loop — the hardware section costs one SQLite read on page render and one write on save.

functional_requirements.title: Hardware section in Settings — OLED display configuration
functional_requirements.description: The hardware section also carries an OLED display configuration: enable/disable and which metric the panel shows (cpu / ram / temp / ip). The value persists. Realises the parent's AC-013-003. The panel does NOT write to the OLED — same rationale as FR-082: the owner requires this to stay lightweight on the Pi.
acceptance_criteria: The rendered /settings page's hardware section contains an OLED display configuration with an enable toggle and a metric selector offering cpu, ram, temp and ip.
Saving the OLED configuration persists both the enabled flag and the selected metric; a subsequent page load renders them, surviving a process restart.
An OLED metric outside the four allowed values is rejected with HTTP 400 and the stored value is unchanged.
Saving without a valid CSRF token is rejected with HTTP 403 and nothing is persisted.
Saving or reading the OLED configuration performs no hardware I/O and starts no background loop.

user_personas.goal: Run a headless Raspberry Pi at home and know, from one browser panel, what it is doing — and act on it (restart a unit, read its logs, take a backup) without opening a terminal.
user_personas.pain_point: Alert storms wake them at 3am for an outage they are already handling; the only backup they can download is unencrypted; reading a failing unit's logs means leaving the panel and using the page-level log dropdown or SSHing in.

no_go_zone: Physically driving the Pironman fan (PWM/GPIO) or writing pixels to the OLED panel — FR-082/FR-083 deliver the control surface and its persistence only. The owner explicitly required this on 2026-07-13: a previous hardware-control attempt cost the Pi significant CPU and memory, and it cannot be verified in CI. Actuating the hardware is deferred and must be declared as technical debt in Phase 4.
Any polling loop, daemon connection or per-request hardware I/O introduced by the hardware section — it must cost one SQLite read on render and one write on save, nothing more.

Listing prior backups and downloading the stored encrypted file (parent AC-015-004) — deferred by the owner on 2026-07-13. AC-015-004 therefore stays untested after this feature; it is tracked in the backlog. The existing GET /api/settings/backup snapshot route is untouched.
Restoring or deleting a backup from Settings — follows from the deferral above.
Per-rule, per-source or per-severity mute — FR-079 is a single global window of exactly 1h / 4h / 24h, as the parent AC-005-005 specifies. No custom durations.
Muting email or any channel other than Telegram — the parent AC scopes mute to Telegram delivery.
Digest scheduling beyond a single daily hour — no weekly, custom-cron, or per-severity digest.
Streaming or tailing logs live in the drawer — FR-081 is a one-shot fetch of the last 100 lines, not a follow.
constraints: Go + HTMX + Tailwind, no SPA framework and no new frontend runtime dependency.
Privilege separation is mandatory: any host-level action goes through the ultron-helper Unix socket, never a direct exec from the panel process.
SQLite is the only datastore; new persisted state extends the existing schema via the migration path already in internal/database.
Runs on a Raspberry Pi: no polling loop or fan-out that would be expensive on ARM with limited RAM.
The settings page carries no page-level inline <script> — client behaviour lives in web/static/js/settings.js and the widget files (CSS7).
technology_preferences: Reuse internal/notify's existing SMTP notifier for the digest rather than a second mail path.
Reuse privileged.SystemLogs(ctx, source, 100) for the drawer — the 100-line fetch already exists.
Reuse encryptFileAESGCM / the ULTRONENC2 format for backups; the download path only reads what the backup writer already produced.
Reuse the settings widget vocabulary (segmented, toggle, chip-preset, stepper) for the new controls so the hardware section binds through the existing settings.js controller.

original_brief:
## Feature
Build the six behaviors the approved requirements already promise but the product never implemented: a Telegram mute window, a daily email digest, a per-service log drawer, a hardware section in Settings (fan mode + OLED display), and a backup list with encrypted download.

## Problem / Why
`aitri verify-complete` gates on acceptance-criteria coverage. An audit of the main pipeline (BL-033) found 41 acceptance criteria with no test. 35 turned out to be real behaviors that were merely untested (now covered) — but 6 traced to behavior the requirements demand and the code never grew:

- **AC-005-005** — the admin can pick a mute window (1h / 4h / 24h); no Telegram message is sent while it is open. Nothing in `internal/notify` implements mute/silence; the only suppression is the 60s storm coalescing window (FR-024), which is a different mechanism.
- **AC-006-004** — with the daily digest enabled, one email summarising the last 24h of alerts is sent at the digest hour. `grep -ri digest internal/` returns nothing.
- **AC-010-002** — a service row opens a log drawer showing the last 100 lines from journalctl. The substance exists (`handleFetchSystemLogs` → `privileged.SystemLogs(ctx, source, 100)` → `journalctl -u <unit> -n 100`), but only as the page-level `/logs` dropdown; service rows have no drawer.
- **AC-013-002 / AC-013-003** — the Settings page shows a hardware section with a fan-mode selector and an OLED display configuration. No hardware section exists at all.
- **AC-015-004** — Settings lists prior backups and clicking download delivers the encrypted file. The encryption primitive exists (`encryptFileAESGCM`, ULTRONENC2, exercised by `backup_crypto_test.go`) and the automated backup flow uses it, but the only download route (`GET /api/settings/backup`) makes a FRESH plaintext SQLite snapshot and serves it as `application/x-sqlite3`. Prior backups are neither listed nor downloadable.

[ASSUMPTION] The user's intent is that these six ship as originally specified, not that the requirements were aspirational — confirmed on 2026-07-13 when they chose "implement all six via the feature pipeline" over amending the requirements.

## Target Users
The single admin operating the Raspberry Pi panel. No new user types.

## New Behavior
- The system must let the admin open a mute window of 1h, 4h or 24h, and must suppress Telegram sends for its duration, resuming automatically when it expires.
- The system must let the admin enable a daily digest with a digest hour, and must send exactly one email at that hour summarising the previous 24h of alerts.
- The system must let the admin open a log drawer on any systemd service row, showing the last 100 journalctl lines for that unit, fetched through the privileged helper.
- The system must render a hardware section in Settings containing a fan-mode selector and an OLED display configuration, persisting both.
- The system must list prior backups in Settings, and must deliver the stored encrypted backup file (not a fresh plaintext snapshot) when the admin clicks download.

## Success Criteria
- GIVEN a 1h mute window is open, WHEN an alert fires, THEN no Telegram message is sent; WHEN the window expires, THEN sends resume. (AC-005-005)
- GIVEN the daily digest is enabled, WHEN the digest hour is reached, THEN exactly one email summarising the last 24h of alerts is sent. (AC-006-004)
- GIVEN a systemd service row, WHEN the admin opens its log drawer, THEN the last 100 journalctl lines for that unit are shown. (AC-010-002)
- GIVEN the Settings page, WHEN the hardware section renders, THEN a fan-mode selector and an OLED display configuration are present and persist. (AC-013-002, AC-013-003)
- GIVEN Settings lists prior backups, WHEN the admin clicks download, THEN the encrypted backup file is delivered to the browser. (AC-015-004)
- `aitri verify-complete` passes with zero untested acceptance criteria.

## Touch Points
MODIFIES:
- FR-005 (Telegram) — `internal/notify/dispatcher.go`, `internal/notify/telegram.go`: consult the mute window before sending.
- FR-006 (Email) — `internal/notify/email.go` + a new digest scheduler.
- FR-010 (Logs) — `internal/server/handlers_system.go` (`handleFetchSystemLogs` already fetches 100 lines), `web/templates/partials/services-list.html`.
- FR-013 (Hardware) — `web/templates/partials/` (new `settings-hardware.html`), `internal/server/templates.go`, `internal/server/handlers_settings.go`.
- FR-015 (Backup) — `internal/server/handlers_performance.go` (`handleSettingsBackup` currently serves a plaintext snapshot), `web/templates/partials/settings-maintenance.html`.
- `internal/database/` — new persisted config for mute window, digest hour, fan mode, OLED.
- `scripts/aitri-test.sh` + `spec/03_TEST_CASES.json` — new TC emit lines traced by `ac_id`.

PURELY ADDS: backup listing endpoint, digest scheduler, log-drawer endpoint.

## Must Not Break (Regression Boundary)
- Telegram alerts (FR-005) keep sending immediately when NO mute window is open; the FR-024 60s storm coalescing keeps working independently of mute.
- Per-event email alerts (FR-006) keep sending on every fire; the digest is additive, not a replacement.
- The `/logs` page (FR-010) keeps working as a page-level source dropdown.
- Every existing Settings section (alerts, telegram, email, performance, backup, maintenance, system controls) keeps saving; the accordion, form-state pills, widgets and CSRF gating (FR-057..FR-070) keep working, including after hx-boost swaps.
- The privileged helper (FR-011) keeps validating every unit name against its allow-list; no new host action bypasses the Unix socket.
- Backups stay encrypted at rest (AC-015-003) and the automated schedule keeps running; the existing `GET /api/settings/backup` snapshot path must not start leaking an unencrypted file to a new caller.
- All 80 currently-passing test cases keep passing.

## Out of Scope
- Physically driving the Pironman fan or writing to the OLED panel (the ACs require the Settings controls and their persistence; actuating the hardware needs the Pironman daemon on the Pi and is deferred — declare it as technical debt).
- Per-rule or per-source mute (the AC specifies a global 1h/4h/24h window only).
- Digest scheduling granularity beyond a single daily hour (no weekly/custom cron).
- Backup retention/pruning changes — the existing retention job stays as-is.
- Restoring a backup from the listing (download only).
